reason: Elisha (אֱלִישָׁע) is presented as an ordinary, non-divine character with clear agency in this narrative. He is initially depicted performing ordinary labor (plowing with twelve yoke of oxen), yet demonstrates deliberate agency through several actions: he makes a conscious decision to abandon his livelihood and follow Elijah, requests permission to say farewell to his parents, and deliberately sacrifices his oxen (cooking them with his plow as fuel) to feed the people before committing himself to prophetic service. These choices reflect genuine human agency and decision-making independent of divine coercion.
